newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean trade in dark over Chicago talk.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean trade in dark over Chicago talk.

text.p: Brazilian soybean traders were surprised at talk today in the Chicago futures market that Brazilian buyers could be looking to buy 200,000 tonnes U.S. soybeans but did not rule out the possibility.
One trader said some interest had been shown on the part of buyers last week but none had heard of any actual deals.
"I would say that it isn't impossible. But this sort of thing always happens very much under wraps and we only hear about it two weeks later," said Flavio Franca of consultants Safras e Mercado.
Brazil is in between harvests, with Safras estimating earlier this week that as of November 21, only two percent or 387,000 tonnes of the 1995/96 remained to be sold.
Estimates of total imports in the 1996/97 commercial year (February/January) range between 1.3 million tonnes on the part of industry associations to up to two million from some traders.

So far, Brazilian buyers, principally food processors such as Ceval and Sadia, are thought to have bought between 330,000 and 400,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans for delivery this year, with the majority of imports coming from Paraguay.
Ceval and Sadia officials were unavailable to comment on whether they were looking for fresh supply from the U.S.
